issues.description: The problem statement requires a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) to manage deliveries, but the solution implements a static method with a different name (receiveDelivery). This identifier mismatch (acceptSupplyDelivery vs receiveDelivery) will confuse students about which method to implement and will cause tests expecting acceptSupplyDelivery to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Rename the solution method receiveDelivery to acceptSupplyDelivery with the signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity), or update the problem statement and tests to use receiveDelivery everywhere.

issues.description: The problem description instructs students to initialize the SealSaloon stock in the constructor (and describes it as a final Stock), while also requiring the stock attribute to be static. Initializing a static (and final) field in an instance constructor is contradictory and can confuse students about where and how to initialize the shared stock. The solution instead initializes a static final stock at field declaration.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: either require stock to be a static field initialized at declaration or in a static initializer (as in the solution), or require a non-static final stock initialized in the constructor. Update the problem statement to consistently state that stock is static and should be initialized at declaration/static initializer, or change the static requirement if constructor initialization is intended.
